name: Finn McCool
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Finn McCool is a folkloric giant told of in Ireland and in Scotland. Tales of him thrive in both countries, and above all in Ulster, the northern province of Ireland. People view him as a dim copy of the noted Fionn Mac Cumhaill, a leading Irish hero, yet he stands as his own figure, a being of wild energy rather like Paul Bunyan. The famous stories credit him with building the Giant's Causeway, the well-known basalt cliffs, by hurling stones into the sea, and with beating a rival giant named Benadonner by guile. In other tellings Finn kills the giant who raised the causeway.
